note: Verified against museum/auction/press sources on the as_of date. Locations and on-view statuses change — check the museum before you travel.

verification.europe: Re-verified 2026-07-06 with fresh web searches, prioritizing mid-2026 whereabouts, exhibition/loan claims, and prices. CONFIRMED AS WRITTEN: Renoir show exists ('Renoir and Love', Orsay, 17 Mar–19 Jul 2026, with Phillips Collection's Boating Party — its only venue, back in DC from Aug 2026); London Sunflowers loan to Philadelphia 6 Jun–11 Oct 2026 (first Atlantic crossing — National Gallery + Art Newspaper + Philadelphia Museum); 'Van Eyck: The Portraits' 21 Nov 2026–11 Apr 2027, all nine portraits; Girl with a Pearl Earring to Osaka 21 Aug–27 Sep 2026 with Mauritshuis closed 24 Aug–20 Sep (museum press release + CODART); Guernica loan to Bilbao (proposed Oct 2026–Jun 2027) refused April 2026 on fragility grounds; Uffizi Botticelli rehang unveiled 16 Jun 2026 (AP); Louvre €22/€32 non-EEA price since 14 Jan 2026, strikes and 'Nouvelle Renaissance' Mona Lisa room ~2031 (Selldorf Architects); Operation Night Watch varnish removal in public glass chamber; Van Gogh Museum Masterplan 2028 funding fight/mediation with Dutch state; EU sanctioned Hermitage director Piotrovsky 23 Apr 2026 (20th package); Last Supper €15, quarterly blocks (Sep–Dec 2026 on sale 23 Jun 2026), Wednesday-noon extra releases (official site); Sistine Last Judgment cleaning Feb–Easter 2026 behind a full-size reproduction with chapel open; Vatican €20 door/€25 online; Rijksmuseum €25. CORRECTED: (1) Renoir entry — '150th anniversary' belongs to the painting (1876), not the Orsay (opened 1986); rewritten and unverifiable expo.paris source replaced with Orsay/Art Newspaper/Phillips pages. (2) Pearl Earring — exact dates '14 Aug' and 'back 5 Oct' could not be verified anywhere; softened to 'mid-August' and 'early October, confirm at mauritshuis.nl'; '12 years' changed to 'first abroad since 2014' (sources say first Japan visit in 14 years). (3) Accademia price — was '€20 + €4 booking fee'; actually €16 + €4 = €20 total online. (4) MUNCH Scream rotation — 'roughly every hour' is not on the official page, which only says versions rotate during the day; interval claim removed. (5) Guernica — refusal attributed to Reina Sofía AND Spain's culture ministry (April 2026). (6) Sistine — sharpened to verified facts (work began 1 Feb 2026, reproduction covered the fresco, chapel open). (7) Replaced unverified press URLs (two ArtNews Louvre links, a Washington Post Uffizi link, a 2014 Artnet Ophelia link) with URLs verified to exist. FLAGGED: Ophelia downgraded to 'unknown' — Tate's artwork page would not confirm live display status in two fetches and no 2026 loan was found either way; recheck before publish. Room numbers kept only where famously stable (Salle des États, Salle Mollien, Prado 012/056A, Hermitage 254, KHM Room X, Mauritshuis 15 — the last not re-verified this pass). NOT re-verified in depth (stable, low-risk): Orangerie, Prado rooms, Belvedere, KHM, Hamburg (Met Friedrich show ended May 2025; no loan found). MISSING GIANTS for a Europe atlas: Venus de Milo and Winged Victory of Samothrace (Louvre), the Ghent Altarpiece (St Bavo's, Ghent — glaring given the Van Eyck entry), Vermeer's Milkmaid and View of Delft, Raphael's School of Athens (Vatican), Goya's Third of May 1808 (Prado), Michelangelo's Pietà (St Peter's), Klimt/Botticelli covered; Starry Night is correctly absent (MoMA, New York).
verification.world: VERIFIED (fresh web checks, July 6, 2026). CORRECTED — 1) pine-trees-tohaku: REMOVED the claim that Honkan Rooms 2–3 close Dec 14, 2026–Apr 26, 2027; TNM's actual announcement was Rooms 7–10 closed Dec 1, 2025–Apr 7, 2026 (already past) — the dataset's version looked like a fabricated/garbled memory. Jan 1–12, 2026 showing in Honkan Room 2 confirmed via TNM press release. 2) annunciation-el-greco-ohara: reopening date corrected to April 25, 2026 (closure was Feb 9–Apr 24); added verified detail — 2025 restoration (first in ~66 years, Prado conservator), shown in Main Building Room 3 in 'Revived Brilliance of Color' Apr 25, 2026–Mar 28, 2027; dropped the unverified 'annex on long-term closure' clause; added official project/news URLs (checked HTTP 200). 3) adele-bloch-bauer-i: closure (May 27, 2026), autumn-2026 reopening, Met merger (announced May 2026, effective 2028) and 'painting stays in the townhouse' all confirmed; replaced an unverifiable artnews.com URL with The Art Newspaper's verified May 14, 2026 story; neuegalerie.org/womaningold link checked live. 4) viva-la-vida: removed unverified 'it has never left the home'. 5) great-wave-met: rephrased 'several impressions, all in dark storage' to what the live database actually shows (no gallery number, July 2026). 6) les-demoiselles: removed unverified 'ongoing hang since 2024'; Gallery 502 confirmed as an ongoing MoMA gallery named for the work; swapped source to the gallery page. 7) irises-getty: W204 confirmed; ADDED the April 2026 announcement that the Getty Center closes Mar 15, 2027 for ~11 months (reopen spring 2028). 8) rosa-e-azul-masp: tour dates tightened to Mar 10–May 10, 2026 (Casa Fiat, Belo Horizonte); 'stayed home for conservation' confirmed by Casa Fiat/press. 9) american-gothic: closure detail refined to Feb 16, 2026, galleries 162–179/265/271 (none of the three AIC icons affected); artic.edu collection-updates source added. 10) spiral-jetty: softened unverified 'waterline nearly a mile away'. 11) along-the-river-qingming: confirmed centenary display Sep 30–Dec 30, 2025, Meridian Gate, first showing since 2015; swapped an unverifiable beijing.gov.cn URL for a checked report. CONFIRMED UNCHANGED (live sources): Washington Crossing Gallery 760 and Great Wave not-on-view (Met API), American Gothic 263 / Nighthawks 262 / Grande Jatte 240 (AIC API is_on_view=true), MoMA Water Lilies Gallery 515 and Persistence of Memory Floor 5 on view, Jadeite Cabbage back in Taipei Gallery 302 since June 12, 2026 (NPM exhibition page), Ginevra de' Benci on view (photographed May 30, 2026; room fluid amid renovations), Salvator Mundi still vanished (nothing newer than the 2024 Geneva report), Blue Poles on display (plus 2025–26 reports NGA refused a several-hundred-million-dollar private offer), Barnes Bonheur de vivre second-floor ensemble, MFA Gauguin in Gallery 255. CAVEATS: moma.org, collections.mfa.org, diaart.org and searchthecollection.nga.gov.au block automated fetchers (HTTP 403), so those on-view statements rest on the museums' Google-indexed pages, named gallery pages, and secondary press rather than a live database read. MISSING GIANTS to consider for this Americas/Asia-Pacific batch: The Two Fridas (Museo de Arte Moderno, Mexico City — arguably Kahlo's most famous painting), Diego Rivera's Detroit Industry murals (DIA) or Man, Controller of the Universe (Bellas Artes), Wyeth's Christina's World and Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans (MoMA), the Meat-Shaped Stone (Taipei NPM, pairs with the Cabbage), Ogata Kōrin's Irises screens (Nezu Museum, Tokyo), Sidney Nolan's Ned Kelly series (NGA Canberra), and nothing from Canada (e.g., Tom Thomson's The Jack Pine, Ottawa). No European entries at all — flagging in case that scope is unintentional.

works.title: Mona Lisa
works.on_view: on view — still in the Salle des États; a dedicated gallery beneath the Cour Carrée (Selldorf Architects) is planned for ~2031 under the 'Louvre Nouvelle Renaissance' project
works.access_note: Timed ticket required: €22 (EEA) / €32 (non-EEA, since 14 Jan 2026); book at louvre.fr; closed Tuesdays. Staff strikes closed the museum repeatedly in 2025–26 — check the site on the day.
works.why: The world's most famous portrait — Leonardo's smoke-soft smile has been drawing crowds since it hung in the bathroom of a French king.

image.license: Public domain (PD-Art; artist Leonardo da Vinci d. 1519)

works.title: Liberty Leading the People
works.on_view: on view — back since May 2024, after a six-month restoration stripped eight layers of yellowed varnish and recovered the original blues and greys
works.access_note: Included in the Louvre timed ticket (€22 EEA / €32 non-EEA); book at louvre.fr; closed Tuesdays.
works.why: Delacroix's bare-breasted Marianne on the barricade became the face of revolution — and of the French Republic itself.

works.title: The Raft of the Medusa
works.on_view: on view — hangs in the red Salle Mollien among the giant canvases of French Romanticism; far too large and fragile to travel
works.access_note: Included in the Louvre timed ticket (€22 EEA / €32 non-EEA); book at louvre.fr; closed Tuesdays.
works.why: Géricault turned a fresh shipwreck scandal into a seven-metre history painting — journalism made monumental.

works.title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
works.on_view: on view — central to the Orsay's 'Renoir and Love' exhibition (17 Mar–19 Jul 2026), staged as the painting turns 150, shown near Luncheon of the Boating Party on rare loan from Washington's Phillips Collection; back to the permanent galleries after 19 July
works.access_note: Museum ticket, book at musee-orsay.fr; closed Mondays.
works.why: Impressionism at full tilt — dappled Sunday light on a Montmartre dance, painted as if in passing.

works.title: Water Lilies (Nymphéas) cycle
works.medium: Oil on canvas — eight mural panels
works.room: The two oval Nymphéas rooms, built to Monet's design
works.on_view: on view — permanently installed in the oval rooms Monet planned for them; no renovation closure found as of mid-2026
works.access_note: Museum ticket, book at musee-orangerie.fr; closed Tuesdays.
works.why: Monet's parting gift to France — a horizonless loop of water and sky he offered as a refuge for 'overworked nerves'.

image.license: Public domain (PD-Art; Monet d. 1926, within the 1955 cutoff)

works.title: The Night Watch
works.room: Night Watch Gallery, at the end of the Gallery of Honour
works.on_view: on view — under live restoration: displayed in a glass chamber while the Operation Night Watch team removes the varnish applied after the 1975 attack; visitors watch the conservators work
works.access_note: €25 adult timed ticket (under-18s free), online only at rijksmuseum.nl; open daily 9–17.
works.why: The group portrait that broke its genre — a militia caught mid-stride, in motion and in light.

works.title: Sunflowers (1889)
works.on_view: on view — declared too fragile ever to travel again (2019), so it never leaves Amsterdam; the museum is open, though a €104m 'Masterplan 2028' renovation is planned from 2028 amid a funding fight (now legal action and mediation) with the Dutch state
works.access_note: Timed-entry ticket, online only at vangoghmuseum.nl; sells out days ahead in summer.
works.why: Yellow on yellow on yellow — the bouquet Van Gogh painted to welcome Gauguin, now painting's best-known still life.

works.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
works.on_view: on view — until mid-August 2026, then traveling: shown at the Nakanoshima Museum of Art, Osaka, 21 Aug–27 Sep 2026 (her first trip abroad since 2014) while the Mauritshuis closes for building work 24 Aug–20 Sep; back on her wall in The Hague by early October — confirm exact days at mauritshuis.nl
works.access_note: Museum ticket, book at mauritshuis.nl; check dates around the late-summer 2026 closure and the Japan loan.
works.why: A glance over the shoulder and one dot of white on a pearl — the quietest famous painting in the world.

works.title: The Birth of Venus
works.on_view: on view — rehung 16 June 2026 in the Uffizi's reordered, grey-walled Botticelli rooms, now in an airtight case facing the Primavera across adjoining spaces
works.access_note: Timed ticket via uffizi.it (official reseller B-ticket); summer slots sell out — book ahead; closed Mondays.
works.why: Venus on her shell — the Renaissance rediscovering the classical nude, drawn with a goldsmith's line.

works.title: Primavera (Spring)
works.on_view: on view — part of the same 16 June 2026 rearrangement, hung opposite The Birth of Venus in an adjoining room, in a new airtight case
works.access_note: Timed ticket via uffizi.it; book ahead in high season; closed Mondays.
works.why: Nine mythological figures in an orange grove — spring turned into philosophy for the Medici.

works.title: David
works.room: The Tribune — the skylit apse built for him in 1873
works.on_view: on view — permanent centrepiece of the museum
works.access_note: €16 + €4 booking fee (€20 total booked online); reserve 2–4 weeks ahead via galleriaaccademiafirenze.it (official) — early slots sell out first; closed Mondays; free first Sunday of the month.
works.why: Seventeen feet of marble resolve — the Republic of Florence carved as a young giant-killer.

image.license: CC0 (Rijksmuseum dedication of a 19th-century Brogi albumen print; sculpture itself PD, Michelangelo d. 1564)

works.title: Sistine Chapel ceiling and The Last Judgment
works.on_view: on view — the Last Judgment had extraordinary cleaning from 1 Feb 2026 (its first in 30 years), hidden behind a full-size reproduction while the chapel stayed open; work was scheduled to finish by Easter and no ongoing works are reported as of July 2026
works.access_note: Entry only with a Vatican Museums ticket — €20 at the door, €25 booked online at museivaticani.va (recommended; queues are long); the chapel is the visit's final stop.
works.why: The Creation of Adam's almost-touching fingers — a ceiling that reset the measure of what one painter could do.

works.title: Las Meninas
works.room: Room 012 — its longtime home at the heart of the Velázquez galleries
works.on_view: on view — in its usual place
works.access_note: General admission via museodelprado.es; the Prado offers free entry in its final opening hours each day (check the schedule); closed only a few holidays.
works.why: Painting about painting — Velázquez steps behind his canvas and pulls the viewer into the royal family.

works.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
works.on_view: on view — a fixed point of the Prado's Bosch room; it does not travel
works.access_note: General admission via museodelprado.es; free final-hours entry daily (check schedule).
works.why: Eden to orgy to hell across three panels — five centuries on, still the strangest picture in any museum.

works.title: Guernica
works.museum: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía
works.on_view: on view — in April 2026 the Reina Sofía and Spain's culture ministry refused a proposed Oct 2026–Jun 2027 loan to the Guggenheim Bilbao for the bombing's 90th anniversary, after a conservation report judged the canvas too fragile for any transport; it stays in Madrid
works.access_note: Museum ticket via museoreinasofia.es; free-entry slots most evenings and Sunday afternoons.
works.why: The twentieth century's scream against war — painted in weeks for the 1937 Paris fair after the bombing of Gernika.
works.image_note: Under copyright: Picasso died 1973, so 70 years p.m.a. runs to 2044. Not public domain anywhere we serve; no image provided.

works.title: Sunflowers (1888)
works.on_view: traveling — on loan to the Philadelphia Museum of Art 6 June–11 October 2026 ('Van Gogh's Sunflowers: A Symphony in Blue and Yellow'), its first-ever Atlantic crossing; normally in the free collection displays and back in London in autumn 2026
works.access_note: Collection entry is free when the painting is home; nationalgallery.org.uk.
works.why: The Arles original of the yellow bouquet — brightness itself, painted to greet Gauguin's arrival.

works.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
works.on_view: on view — and set to anchor the Gallery's own 'Van Eyck: The Portraits' exhibition, 21 Nov 2026–11 Apr 2027, uniting all nine surviving Van Eyck portraits for the first time
works.access_note: Free with the permanent collection; the 2026–27 Van Eyck exhibition will be ticketed; nationalgallery.org.uk.
works.why: A convex mirror, a signature on the wall, a held hand — oil painting's founding document of everyday intimacy.

works.title: Ophelia
works.on_view: unknown — normally a fixture of the free collection displays and no 2026 loan was found, but Tate's live 'on display' status could not be confirmed at verification time; check the Tate artwork page before visiting
works.access_note: Free; Tate Britain (Millbank) open daily; tate.org.uk.
works.why: Shakespeare's drowning girl painted flower by flower from a Surrey riverbank — Pre-Raphaelite devotion in full.

works.title: The Kiss
works.medium: Oil and gold leaf on canvas
works.on_view: on view — on continuous display at the Upper Belvedere in the Vienna 1900 galleries; the Belvedere does not lend it
works.access_note: Timed ticket for the Upper Belvedere, book at belvedere.at; quietest at opening or late afternoon.
works.why: Two lovers dissolving into a field of gold — Vienna 1900's icon of tenderness.

works.title: The Tower of Babel
works.room: Room X (the Bruegel Room), Picture Gallery
works.on_view: on view — permanent anchor of the world's largest Bruegel collection (twelve panels)
works.access_note: Museum ticket, book at khm.at.
works.why: Babel built as a crumbling colosseum — human ambition audited brick by brick.

works.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
works.on_view: on view — home in Hamburg after the 2024–25 Friedrich anniversary tour (its Met debut closed May 2025); no current loan found
works.access_note: Museum ticket at hamburger-kunsthalle.de; closed Mondays.
works.why: A lone figure above the mist, back turned to us — Romanticism's emblem of the sublime.

works.title: The Scream (1893)
works.on_view: on view — the famous 1893 painted version hangs in the National Museum's Munch room; across town, the MUNCH museum shows its own painting, drawing and lithographs of the motif in rotation, one at a time to protect them from light
works.access_note: National Museum ticket at nasjonalmuseet.no; at MUNCH (munch.no) one Scream is always on display, rotated through the day — a version will be visible whenever you visit.
works.why: A figure on a bridge under a blood-red sky — modern anxiety given a face the whole world knows.

image.license: Public domain (PD-Art; Munch d. 1944, 70y p.m.a. expired 2015)

works.title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
works.on_view: on view — the museum operates normally, but it is effectively hard to reach for most Western visitors: war-related sanctions (the EU sanctioned director Mikhail Piotrovsky in April 2026), no direct flights from the EU/US, and foreign Visa/Mastercard cards do not work in Russia
works.access_note: Russia requires a visa (an e-visa is available to many nationalities); the Hermitage's online shop cannot take foreign cards because of sanctions — buy at ticket offices/machines in roubles or via Russian payment channels.
works.why: Rembrandt's last word on mercy — a father's hands on a kneeling son, painted in the shadow of his own death.

works.title: The Last Supper
works.museum: Museo del Cenacolo Vinciano, Santa Maria delle Grazie
works.room: Refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie
works.on_view: on view — permanently, since it is painted on the refectory wall; entry limited to groups of 40 for 15 minutes in a climate-controlled room
works.access_note: Reservation is mandatory: €15 via the official cenacolovinciano.org; tickets are released in quarterly blocks and sell out within minutes (the Sep–Dec 2026 block opened 23 June 2026) — book 2–4 months ahead; small extra releases every Wednesday at noon; arrive 30 min early; closed Mondays.
works.why: The instant after 'one of you will betray me' — twelve reactions rippling down a table, fading and immortal at once.

works.title: The Starry Night
works.on_view: on view — fifth-floor collection galleries (1880s–1940s); MoMA lists it among its 'Unmissables' and it rarely leaves the building
works.access_note: Timed general-admission ticket; book at moma.org
works.why: Painted from an asylum window at Saint-Rémy, it turned one turbulent night into the most recognized sky in art.

works.title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
works.on_view: on view — fifth floor, in an ongoing collection gallery MoMA names for the painting (Gallery 502: Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon)
works.access_note: Timed general-admission ticket; book at moma.org
works.why: Five fractured figures that broke painting open in 1907 — modern art's founding shock, at MoMA since 1939.
works.image_note: Under copyright: Picasso died 1973, fails the died-1955-or-earlier test (70y p.m.a. runs to 2044). Refused.

works.title: The Persistence of Memory
works.on_view: on view — fifth-floor collection galleries (MoMA's database places it on Floor 5); at MoMA continuously since 1934, though visitors are often surprised how small it is
works.access_note: Timed general-admission ticket; book at moma.org
works.why: Dalí's soft watches, barely larger than a postcard, made time itself melt into a dream.
works.image_note: Under copyright: Dali died 1989, fails the died-1955-or-earlier test (70y p.m.a. runs to 2060). Refused.

works.title: Water Lilies (triptych)
works.medium: oil on canvas, three panels (12.7 m wide overall)
works.room: Gallery 515, Floor 5 — a room MoMA names for the work
works.on_view: on view — Gallery 515, an ongoing room built around the triptych
works.access_note: Timed general-admission ticket; book at moma.org
works.why: Monet's late pond wraps a whole room in water and light — painting as immersion, decades before installation art.

works.title: Washington Crossing the Delaware
works.medium: oil on canvas (the Met's largest painting on canvas)
works.on_view: on view — Gallery 760, American Wing (confirmed in the Met's collection database, July 2026), in a reconstruction of its original gilded trophy frame
works.access_note: General-admission ticket (pay-what-you-wish for New York State residents); metmuseum.org
works.why: The grand image of America's origin story, painted at the scale of opera and endlessly recast ever since.

works.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
works.medium: polychrome woodblock print, ink and color on paper
works.on_view: not on view — the Met's celebrated impression shows no gallery location in the collection database (checked July 2026); like most Japanese prints it is light-sensitive and surfaces only in brief rotations
works.access_note: Included with Met admission when a rotation brings it out; check the object page or Asian Art galleries schedule before visiting
works.why: The most reproduced wave in the world: Prussian blue, a distant Fuji, and thirty centimeters of fragile paper.

works.title: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I (Woman in Gold)
works.medium: oil, silver and gold leaf on canvas
works.on_view: not on view — the Neue Galerie closed for construction on May 27, 2026 and reopens in autumn 2026, in time for its 25th anniversary; under the merger with the Met announced in May 2026 (to take effect in 2028), the painting is to remain in the Fifth Avenue townhouse
works.access_note: Museum closed until autumn 2026; reopening details at neuegalerie.org
works.why: Klimt's gilded icon, restituted from Nazi-looted history and brought to New York in 2006 for a then-record $135 million.

works.title: Ginevra de' Benci
works.on_view: on view — West Building main floor (photographed on view as recently as late May 2026); during the building's rolling renovations it has moved between rooms, so check nga.gov for the current room
works.access_note: Free — no ticket required; nga.gov
works.why: The only Leonardo painting on public view in the Americas — a portrait made decades before the Mona Lisa.

works.title: American Gothic
works.on_view: on view — Gallery 263 (confirmed in the museum's collection database, July 2026); unaffected by the gallery closures that began Feb 16, 2026 (galleries 162–179, 265 and 271) for the Grainger Center construction
works.access_note: General-admission ticket; artic.edu
works.why: A pitchfork, a Gothic window, and two unreadable faces — the most argued-over image of rural America.

image.license: Public domain (PD-Art; PD-old-70 and US 95-year term expired 2026-01-01)

works.title: Nighthawks
works.on_view: on view — Gallery 262 (confirmed in the museum's collection database, July 2026), steps from American Gothic
works.access_note: General-admission ticket; artic.edu
works.why: Hopper's all-night diner distilled urban loneliness into one pane of glass and fluorescent light.
works.image_note: Under copyright: Edward Hopper died 1967 (after the 1955 cutoff); rights administered by the Whitney Museum / Heirs of Josephine Hopper. No image supplied.

works.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
works.on_view: on view — Gallery 240 (confirmed in the museum's collection database, July 2026), in a reconstruction of the white frame Seurat intended
works.access_note: General-admission ticket; artic.edu
works.why: Seurat's dot-by-dot Sunday afternoon, the manifesto of Pointillism, at home in Chicago since 1924.

works.title: Le Bonheur de vivre (The Joy of Life)
works.on_view: on view — hung in a second-floor gallery within Dr. Barnes's fixed collection 'ensembles', which by the foundation's rules stay essentially unchanged; it returned to the galleries after a 2024 special exhibition at the Barnes
works.access_note: Timed-entry ticket, book ahead; barnesfoundation.org
works.why: Matisse's pastoral of pure color scandalized 1906 Paris and opened the door everything Fauvist and beyond walked through.

works.title: Irises
works.museum: J. Paul Getty Museum, Getty Center
works.on_view: on view — West Pavilion, Gallery W204; the Getty says it is always on view and never travels. Note: the Getty announced in April 2026 that the Getty Center will close March 15, 2027 for roughly a year of renovation
works.access_note: Free with a timed-entry reservation at getty.edu (parking fee applies); plan visits before the Getty Center's renovation closure begins March 15, 2027
works.why: Painted in Van Gogh's first week at the Saint-Rémy asylum; once violet, its irises faded to the blue we love now.

works.title: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
works.on_view: on view — the MFA's gallery page for Gallery 255 ('Impressionism and Beyond', the Rabb Gallery) names it among the works shown there; a 2026–27 banner commission by Joiri Minaya responds to it elsewhere in the museum
works.access_note: General-admission ticket; mfa.org
works.why: Gauguin's Tahitian summa, painted as a final testament — he considered it the greatest thing he had ever done.

works.title: Viva la Vida, Watermelons
works.on_view: on view — displayed in the Casa Azul, the house where Kahlo lived, painted it, and died
works.access_note: Timed tickets sold online only and they sell out weeks ahead; boletos.museofridakahlo.org.mx
works.why: Ripe watermelons inscribed 'Viva la Vida' — long live life — signed by Kahlo just days before her death.
works.image_note: Under copyright: Frida Kahlo d.1954 is a Mexican artist, so the 100-year post-mortem term applies (in copyright until 2055). No image supplied.

works.title: Rosa e Azul — As Meninas Cahen d'Anvers (Pink and Blue)
works.museum: Museu de Arte de São Paulo Assis Chateaubriand (MASP)
works.on_view: on view — MASP keeps its best-loved Renoir in São Paulo: for conservation it stayed home when the museum's other Renoirs toured Casa Fiat de Cultura, Belo Horizonte (Mar 10–May 10, 2026); normally shown in the collection display on Lina Bo Bardi's crystal easels — hangs rotate, so confirm at masp.org.br
works.access_note: Ticketed, book at masp.org.br; Tuesdays are traditionally free
works.why: Renoir's Cahen d'Anvers sisters in pink and blue — Brazil's most cherished painting, floating mid-air on Bo Bardi's glass easels.

works.title: Pine Trees (Shōrin-zu byōbu)
works.medium: pair of six-panel folding screens; ink on paper (National Treasure)
works.on_view: not on view — this light-sensitive National Treasure appears only in short rotations, traditionally at New Year; last shown Jan 1–12, 2026 in the Honkan Room 2 National Treasure Gallery
works.access_note: General-admission ticket when displayed; check the rotation calendar at tnm.jp before going
works.why: Mist, ink, and emptiness — Tōhaku's pines are often called the summit of Japanese ink painting.

works.title: The Annunciation
works.on_view: on view — freshly restored (2025, its first restoration in about 66 years, led by a Prado conservator) and shown in Main Building Room 3 in the feature 'El Greco's The Annunciation: Revived Brilliance of Color' (Apr 25, 2026–Mar 28, 2027); the museum reopened April 25, 2026 after a closure that began Feb 9
works.access_note: General-admission ticket at the door; ohara.or.jp
works.why: An El Greco altarpiece in a canal town — bought in 1922 for Japan's first museum of Western art, and still its heart.

works.title: Jadeite Cabbage with Insects
works.room: Gallery 302, Exhibition Hall I (its traditional Taipei home)
works.on_view: on view — back in Gallery 302 at the Taipei (Northern) branch since June 12, 2026, after a spring showing at the Southern Branch in Chiayi (Mar 5–Jun 7, 2026); it rotates between branches and occasionally travels abroad, so confirm before going
works.access_note: General-admission ticket; current location always posted at npm.gov.tw
works.why: A bok choy carved from a single flawed jade stone, a katydid hidden in its leaves — Taiwan's most adored object.

works.title: Along the River During the Qingming Festival
works.medium: handscroll; ink and light color on silk, 5.28 m long
works.on_view: not on view — the fragile 900-year-old silk scroll is unrolled only for rare special exhibitions; last shown fully unrolled Sept 30–Dec 30, 2025 in the Meridian Gate Gallery for the Palace Museum's centenary, its first public display since 2015. The Song original is in Beijing; the famous versions at Taipei's National Palace Museum are later Ming/Qing reinterpretations
works.access_note: Forbidden City entry by advance online reservation (ID/passport required); the scroll itself can only be seen during rare special exhibitions
works.why: Five metres of Song-dynasty city life — hundreds of figures, boats, and bridges on silk; China's most famous painting.

works.title: Salvator Mundi
works.museum: None — bought for display at Louvre Abu Dhabi (announced 2017), never exhibited there or anywhere since
works.city: Unknown — reported in 2024 to be in storage in Geneva; earlier reports placed it on a Saudi yacht
works.on_view: unknown — not seen in public since its record $450.3M sale at Christie's in November 2017; Louvre Abu Dhabi has said it does not know its whereabouts, and the most recent credible reports (2024) point to Geneva storage, with speculation about a future museum in Riyadh; nothing newer confirmed as of July 2026
works.access_note: Cannot currently be seen anywhere; no museum displays it
works.why: The most expensive artwork ever auctioned vanished from public view the moment the hammer fell.

works.title: Blue Poles (Number 11, 1952)
works.medium: enamel and aluminium paint with glass on canvas
works.on_view: on view — on permanent display after major conservation during the 2020 closure; the NGA calls it its most-viewed work, rarely off display since 1982 (the gallery recently rebuffed a private offer of several hundred million dollars for it)
works.access_note: Free general admission; nga.gov.au
works.why: The drip painting whose A$1.3M price scandalized 1973 Australia — and became the young nation's proudest purchase.
works.image_note: Under copyright: Jackson Pollock died 1956 (after the 1955 cutoff); rights via ARS/Pollock-Krasner Foundation. No image supplied.

works.title: Spiral Jetty
works.museum: Dia Art Foundation (in situ at Rozel Point, Great Salt Lake)
works.city: Rozel Point, Box Elder County, Utah
works.medium: black basalt rock, salt crystals, and earth; a 1,500-foot coil in the lake
works.on_view: on view — continuously exposed since 2002; the receded Great Salt Lake usually leaves the coil fully out of the water, though how far the waterline sits varies year to year
works.access_note: Free and always open, no ticket or booking; a remote drive from Salt Lake City with the last ~16 miles on unpaved road and no facilities — visitor guidance at diaart.org
works.why: Land art's defining monument: a basalt spiral drawn into a pink inland sea, changing with every drought and flood.
works.image_note: Under copyright: Robert Smithson died 1973 (Holt/Smithson Foundation, VAGA/ARS). Additionally an earthwork/sculpture, so any photograph carries separate photographer rights. No image supplied.
